scenes.title: What Deliberation Is About
scenes.summary: The adviser deals only with goods and evils that can come about or not and whose origin lies in us; no one deliberates about what is necessary or impossible, or about what nature or chance brings.

scenes.title: Capacities, Not Sciences
scenes.summary: A precise survey of public business belongs to a truer science, politics. Rhetoric is made of analytics and of the political study of characters, like dialectic in part and sophistry in part; to turn these capacities into sciences of particular subjects is to destroy their nature.

scenes.title: Five Subjects; Revenue
scenes.summary: The chief subjects of deliberation are five: revenue, war and peace, the defense of the country, imports and exports, and legislation. On revenue the adviser must know the city's income and expenses, and what others have found out.

scenes.title: War and Peace
scenes.summary: He must know the city's forces, actual and potential, the wars it has fought, and the forces of its neighbors and likely enemies, so as to keep peace with the stronger and choose war with the weaker; and he must study the outcomes of others' wars.

scenes.title: Defense and Food
scenes.summary: On defense he must know the garrison and its posts; on food, what the city produces and imports, and what it must export, so that treaties may be made and the citizens kept free of complaint toward the stronger and the useful.

scenes.title: Legislation
scenes.summary: The safety of the city lies in its laws, so the adviser must know the kinds of constitution and how each is destroyed by relaxing or overstraining, as a nose too hooked or too snub ceases to look like a nose. Travelers' descriptions of the earth and histories help; but all this is the work of politics, not of rhetoric.
